new_statements.quote: All four Maiduan languages have basically the same uncomplicated phonology (Table 32). In all four languages there are two full sets of oral stops, plain (p, t, c, k) and glottalized (p', t', c' k') ... contrast short and long vowels. Nisenan consistently places stress on initial syllables; in the other Maiduan languages the placement of stress is unpredictable. Nouns and independent pronouns must always be inflected for case.

Sec. 3.24 'Maiduan Languages' (3.24.1 Konkow, 3.24.2 Chico Maidu, 3.24.3 Northeastern Maidu.. linguistic sketch with Table 32), pp. 136ff; bibliography entries Gatschet 1877d, 1879b; Merriam vocabulary list U-20a.

Reading matches the words but the evidence is family-sketch level (and in tension with Ultan 1967 on Konkow). | checker: Golla 2011 is Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description entry for vall1252; archive.org item californiaindian0000goll (lending-only) and Google Books Zul-EAAAQBAJ exist. The saved snippet file in the mirror hold…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level: apart from Nisenan (fixed initial stress), the Maiduan languages - which for Golla include Chico Maidu - have unpredictable (lexically placed) word stress; no Chico-specific detail.

new_statements.identity_note: Golla treats Chico Maidu (= Glottolog vall1252, his sec. 3.24.2, attested by Gatschet 1877d/1879b at Michopdo on Bidwell's Ranch and by Merriam's Mitchopdo vocabulary) as one of 'four closely related Maiduan languages'; the stress sentence generalises over 'the other Maiduan languages' (i.e. Konkow, Chico Maidu, Northeastern Maidu) after singling out Nisenan. It is a family-level, secondhand statement by the Glottolog's most extensive description author, not a first-hand analysis of Chico Maidu data; our bibliography lists Golla 2011 as 'read: silent' because only 9 front-matter pages and sec. 3.24.2 snippets had been seen - sec. 3.24's linguistic sketch had not been reached. | Family-level paragraph: lists Chico Maidu among the four Maiduan languages, then gives a (Proto-)Maiduan sound inventory (after Ultan 1964) ending '.. vowel length; phonemic stress'. Whether 'phonemic stress' is asserted for each daughter including Chico Maidu or for the proto-language is not decidable from the snippet; secondhand either way. Our bibliography has Campbell 2024 as 'snippet only' for the dialect-status sentence, not this one.

sources.citation: Gatschet, Albert S. 1877. Words, sentences and texts from the language of the Otakimme (Otaki) or Indians of Chico, California (Maidu family). Obtained in August and September 1877. Manuscript notebook, ca. 131 pp., National Anthropological Archives, Smithsonian Institution, NAA MS 646-a (digitized for Breath of Life / Recovering Voices, NSF BCS-1561167). Companion: NAA MS 646-b, Maidu/Michopdo linguistic material, Chico Ranch. [= Golla 2011's Gatschet 1877d]
sources.note: Nothing explicit. The notebook is a field vocabulary + elicited sentences + case/verb paradigms + three short interlinear texts; there is no section on sounds, alphabet, phonetics or accent (MS pp. 2-4 are blank; p. 5 opens directly with 'Numerals'; inside covers carry only '646-a'). Every Maidu form is written with acute accent marks (e.g. p.5 wukte, pene, sa'pe with accents; p.91 mopa'ki, ole'lki butu'; p.97 pi'ni ni'hai 'I hear'; p.129 Ni'seki hullu'ku wi'kni pe'neke..), i.e. primary word-stress DATA for Chico (Valley) Maidu, but no rule statement.
